_comment: Navigation sweep profile for Tetris (1989) (Nintendo) - PRD Part A slice
F14.17, the ADR-0239 selector sweep extended to a game the first five did
not cover. Read by scripts/record_navigation_sweep.py.
RUNG 1, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THIS GAME. navigation.kind is
'input', so no cheat rides with any session, no address is pinned, and
every session is an ADR-0184 s2 clean pass that all four of ADR-0183 s1's
surfaces may read. Rung 2 is available here - Data Crystal publishes both
bytes this selector writes, $0047 starting speed level and $0059 B-type
height level - but rung 1 reaches every place they name, so ADR-0239 s1's
ladder stops at the first rung.
TETRIS IS THE SWEEP'S NEGATIVE CASE, and the profile is shaped to say so.
The place this selector reaches is a STARTING LEVEL, not a different
stage: the same well, the same seven tetrominoes and the same panels are
played, faster, and the level's own contribution to the art is the piece
palette it picks (and, for B-TYPE, the garbage rows the height pre-fills).
So the values below are the levels and the heights, and the interesting
number is whether a later starting level draws anything the first one does
not - which runs/f1417/tetris/RESULT.md reports without dressing up.
THE SELECTOR, AS THIS ROM SHOWS IT (all read off this dump on 2026-09-26):
title          'PUSH START'. One Start pressed before it arrives skips
the copyright notice (measured: a Start at frame 150 -
2.5 s - lands on the title, so most of the notice is
skippable and the entries use 150 f).
game select    'GAME TYPE' with 'A-TYPE' and 'B-TYPE', and 'MUSIC TYPE'
with 'MUSIC-1/2/3/OFF'. Left/Right picks within a row and
Up/Down moves between the two rows; Start goes on to the
selected type's LEVEL screen.
level screen   'LEVEL' as a 2x5 grid (0-4 over 5-9). Right walks it in
reading order, wrapping 4 -> 5 and clamping on 9; Up/Down
switches rows with the column kept. B-TYPE's screen adds
'HEIGHT' as a 2x3 grid (0-2 over 3-5) BESIDE it, and
there - and only there - the A button does something: it
toggles which of the two grids the d-pad drives, leaving
the other grid's cursor where it was.
levels 10-19   Not on the grid. Holding A down and pressing Start with
it still held starts the game ten levels above the
highlighted one. Measured both ways: a-level19's entry
reads $0047 = 19 at the start of the game, and pressing A
and Start on the SAME frames started nothing at all
($0048 read 0), so the two have to be a sequence.
THE PUBLISHED SOURCES, quoted rather than paraphrased. StrategyWiki,
'Tetris (NES)' (https://strategywiki.org/wiki/Tetris_(NES), retrieved
2026-09-26), 'Game modes': 'A-Type: Endless, choice of starting level (0
through 19), clear 10 lines to advance to the next level.' and 'B-Type:
Clear 25 lines, choice of starting level (0 through 19), and choice of
starting garbage height (0 through 5 ...)'; 'Other options': 'Music: Three
choices of music can be selected before each game'; 'Harder levels: To
start a game from levels 10 through 19, highlight a level from 0 through
9, press and hold [A], and press [Start] to begin a game at a level ten
higher than the one you highlighted.' Data Crystal, 'Tetris (NES):RAM
map' (archived copy of 2018-09-23, the live wiki is behind a JS
challenge): $0047 'starting speed level', $0059 'B-type height level',
$00C1 'game type (marathon = 0, 25lines = 1)', $0048 'Current game phase',
$001A 'number of pieces this poweron', $0046/$004F the left/right and down
autorepeat timers the body's holds rely on.
WHAT THE TWO SOURCES DISAGREE ABOUT, and which one this profile follows.
StrategyWiki's 'choice of starting level (0 through 19)' is right about
the reachable range and wrong about the grid: the screen holds ten
entries, Right clamps on 9 (measured: ten Rights read $0047 = 9), and the
range above 9 exists only through the A-hold trick. That is why there is
no 'level 15' value on the grid - the value list follows the measurement.
THE VALUES, 18 sessions. The selector reaches ten levels on the grid, ten
more through the A-hold trick, two game types and six heights, so the
place space is 2 x 20 x 6. What is swept is: every level the GRID holds
for A-TYPE (0-9), the far end of the extended range the A button adds
(19), every height at B-TYPE level 0 (0-5), and the corner the two grids
compose (B-TYPE level 9 height 5). WHAT IS LEFT OUT, and why: levels
10-18, because 19 is the extreme of the range the A button adds and the
sweep asks whether that range draws anything the grid does not, so 19
answers it for 10-18 as well; and the 110 level x height combinations of
B-TYPE beyond the corner, because level and height are independent knobs
on the same screen and each axis is swept complete on its own - the corner
is there to show they compose, not to enumerate them.
A-TYPE LEVEL 0 IS ALSO THE 'BEFORE'. It is the game's own stage-1 route:
a run that answers every menu with the button that is already selected.
Its entry is mint-stage1.txt - the name scripts/stages/README.md gives a
walk from power-on to a stage's start - and it is recorded twice, once as
the sweep's own a-type-level0 value and once on its own into
runs/f1417/tetris/before/, which is the pack --baseline folds in as the
'before' side of ADR-0239 s5. Those two runs are the sweep's CONTROL: they
are the same route through two separate invocations of the recorder, so a
a-type-level0 session reporting new == 0 is not a failure but the check
that the before really is the game's first place and that the two arms
agree.
NO RAM CHECK IS DECLARED, AND THAT IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT AN OVERSIGHT.
ADR-0239 s4 reads a check off the session's FINAL state, and a 120 s
Tetris session does not end where it played: the blind body tops out, the
game shows its GAME OVER and its score screen, and it returns to the
title, where the whole game-state block is reset. Measured 2026-09-26 on
the 120 s pilot (runs/f1417/tetris/pilot/): the final state's screenshot is
the title in all three arms tried, $0047 and $0059 read 00, and a
byte-for-byte diff of a played session's final RAM against a session that
never left the title finds 60 bytes - the sound engine ($0680-$06CE) and
the held-button register ($00F7) - and none of them the selector's. A
check on $0047 would therefore read 00 for all 18 values and would be
worse than no check at all: it would look like a gate and measure nothing.
This is Excitebike's case taken to its end - there a race ending returns
$004F to 00, here every place is cleared by the title - and the sweep
answers it the same way ADR-0239 s4 says to: `new` is the gate. The
per-value proof that each session started where its entry asked for lives
in runs/f1417/tetris/RESULT.md as a table read off short recordings of the
same entries, four seconds into the game, while $0047 and $0059 still hold
what the selector wrote.
NO LIVES PIN, so ADR-0239 s3's inert control does not apply: Tetris has no
lives. A game ends by topping out and that is the game's own GAME OVER
(ADR-0184 s4), recorded rather than foreclosed. defaults.cheats is absent
and no process in this sweep is launched with a cheat at all.
CAVEAT THAT APPLIES TO EVERY SESSION, and it is larger here than in any
other game's profile. A session that has topped out and returned to the
title spends the rest of its 120 s recording the title's own attract
material and its demo game, which the baseline holds too - so a session's
`new` is what its FIRST GAME drew, and the union's growth is bounded by
how much of the 120 s each level spent in play before topping out. The
corollary is the one ADR-0239 s6 states for every game: the stage-clear
transition is never recorded, and here neither is the transition from a
topped-out game back to the title as anything but the title itself.

navigation.label: the title screen's GAME TYPE select (A-TYPE / B-TYPE) and the LEVEL screen behind it (ten grid entries plus the A-hold range above them; B-TYPE's screen adds HEIGHT)
navigation.source: StrategyWiki, 'Tetris (NES)' (https://strategywiki.org/wiki/Tetris_(NES), retrieved 2026-09-26), 'Game modes' and 'Other options': A-Type and B-Type each take a 'choice of starting level (0 through 19)', B-Type adds a 'choice of starting garbage height (0 through 5)', three music choices sit beside them, and levels 10-19 are reached by highlighting 0-9 and pressing Start while A is held. Corroborated by this ROM's own GAME TYPE / LEVEL / HEIGHT screens, read off this dump the same day, and by the bytes the selector writes - $0047 starting speed level, $0059 B-type height level, $00C1 game type - which are Data Crystal's, 'Tetris (NES):RAM map', archived copy of 2018-09-23 (the live wiki is behind a JS challenge). ADR-0239 s1 rung 1: input, no cheat, no pinned address.
